steps.text: Part 4 of 4: The pawn in a busy position. This part covers Check yourself. Each part is short on purpose: finish one, play a game or take a break, and come back.

[H] My guess: the pawn's odd rule (walks straight, attacks sideways) is what lets pawns form chains and walls, the skeleton the other pieces work around. [H] A second guess: most beginner pawn errors come from mixing the walking rule with the capturing rule. Which of the two do you mix up more often?

steps.caption: A walk-through for a new position. Step 1: name the piece. The piece on c2 is a white pawn, so it walks up the board.
Step 2: the forward question. c3 and c4 are both empty and the pawn is on its starting square.

line.say: Both squares were empty, so the jump is available.

steps.caption: Step 3: the diagonal question. The black pawn on b3 can be captured. d3 is empty, so there is nothing to take there, though the pawn still attacks that square.

line.say: The pawn captures diagonally onto the enemy pawn.
The knight recaptures; the white pawn was attacked but it could still move.

steps.caption: Step 4: put both answers together. The pawn has exactly three moves, even though two enemy pieces attack it.
